setlist.title: It Must Have Been the Roses
Why Don't We Do it in the Road

liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Feel Like A Stranger** (2 reviews): A second-set Stranger, which is rarer, followed by a second-set Cumberland Blues; Jerry's solo is singled out as killer, with the rest of the band right on point [21][24]
- **Cumberland Blues** (2 reviews): Phil is monstrous on the low end while Jerry plays at full flight; Jerry's playing on Cumberland is praised as shredding it to pieces [22][23]
- **Jam** (2 reviews): The improvisation reminded the reviewer of a Mind Left Body Jam, though they may be confusing it with the previous night; A trippy jam leads into Drums [16][24]
- **Down in the Bottom** (1 review): Described as smokin', with Bobby sounding strong alongside the rest of the band [23]
- **The Music Never Stopped** (1 review): The song contains a nice, tight jam [24]
- **Gloria** (1 review): Gloria was hot, and Phil tried to steer it into Lovelight, but that transition came later [14]
- **Why Don't We Do it in the Road** (1 review): This was Jerry's version of the song rather than Phil's [14]

## Setlist highlights

- **Down in the Bottom**: back after 120 archived shows (571 days); rare: 10 archived performances [26]
- **we'll be back**: back after 1148 archived shows (5673 days); mythic rare: 2 archived performances [26]
- **preamble**: earliest performance in the archive; mythic rare: 2 archived performances [26]
- **Gloria**: back after 215 archived shows (1114 days) [26]
- **Why Don't We Do it in the Road**: rare: 7 archived performances [26]

## The recordings

- **gd1984-11-03.sbd.greenbereg.powell.21761.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 21 songs; 161 min; rated 1/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd84-11-03.aud.willy-vernon.18111.sbeok.shnf**: audience recording; 20 songs; 152 min; rated 4.25/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: The audience recording sounds excellent; the authorized taping section avoids the hall's trouble spots for sound [15]
- **gd1984-11-03.179943.unknown.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 163 min [4]
- **gd1984-11-03.169045.senn441.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: audience recording; 19 songs; 157 min [6]
- **gd84-11-03.sbd.braverman.8212.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 18 songs; 153 min; rated 4.36/5 by 11 [8]. Said about its sound: The soundboard has digital noise throughout disc 3; the audience source is suggested for post-Drums material; The soundboard is described as a wonderful-sounding show [19][21]

## Around the show

- Berkeley Community Theater has some poor-sounding areas in the auditorium [15]
- Jerry stood playing a descending progression under dark red stage lights [16]
- By the end of the run the band had run low on songs and pulled out oddball covers [20]
- Final night of a six-show Berkeley Community Theater run, with very few songs repeated from earlier nights [14]
- Across the six nights the band tried, with an exception or two, not to repeat songs [16]
- This Why Don't We Do It In The Road was better than the one at the Greek [20]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1984-11-03.sbd.greenbereg.powell.21761.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by John Mollman and Dave Greenberg; source: MSP > D > CD patched with MAC > C > C > D [1]. Also: Soundboard has about 20 seconds from Gloria's end through the start of Why Don't We Do It patched from audience; A 19-second stretch of Uncle John's Band is patched from audience, and a one-second glitch at the end of Space was fixed [1]
- **gd84-11-03.aud.willy-vernon.18111.sbeok.shnf**: source: AUD>MC>DAT>CDR via Raoul Duke, encoded by Willy and Matt Vernon [2]
- **gd1984-11-03.179943.unknown.wiseman.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Scott Wiseman; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Scott Wiseman's Master Audience Cassettes; Unknown mics > Sony TC-D5M (Maxell UDXLII 90) [4]. Also: A soundboard source from Charlie Miller supplies a six-second patch at the start of Deal; Jim Vita's Sennheiser 441 source patches 59 seconds of Drums and 11 seconds of Throwing Stones [4]
- **gd1984-11-03.169045.senn441.vita.miller.clugston.flac2496**: taped by Jim Vita; transferred by Scott Clugston, Charlie Miller; source: Master Audience Cassettes; Sennheiser 441 mics > ?? > Jim Vita's cassettes (Maxell XLII-S) [6]. Also: Doug Lamarre's Sennheiser 441 source supplies Deal, a 1:47 Drums patch, and 9 seconds of the Throwing Stones to Lovelight transition; Joe B. Jones assisted with pitch correction of the recording [6]
- **gd84-11-03.sbd.braverman.8212.sbefail.shnf**: source: SBD> MC> DAT> CD [8]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Steve Schneider Grateful Dead: [1984-11-03 Berkeley Community Theater, Berkeley, CA, USA - Jerry Garcia](https://jerrygarcia.com/show/1984-11-03-berkeley-community-theater-berkeley-ca-usa/) [27]
